note: scripts/move-parser.mjs's function-signature regex had no `macro` alternative, so a public macro fun body was never modelled. FINDINGS-BACK correction: the real ratio is 3 of 4, not 4 of 4 -- MOV-002/004/008 are genuinely re-armed on an idiomatic $-parameter macro; MOV-011 is N/A (a macro has no runtime representation for entry to attach to, so there is no bypass surface to detect). The first fix round's own claim that dropping the $ from a macro param's parsed name was 'cosmetic only' was independently checked and found false for MOV-002: parseBody's multiplications/divisions regexes use \w+, which cannot match a $-led token at all, so $a * $b produced ZERO entries for MOV-002 to iterate -- not a lookup miss against the params table, as first described. Fixed by tolerating a leading $ in parseOneParam's name capture plus the multiplications/divisions regexes; preserving $ in params[].name also fixes a latent false positive (two u128-typed $-params multiplied together used to be flagged anyway). Plus the earlier one-line depth-clamp in parseParams so a lambda-typed macro param (`|u64| -> u64`) doesn't drive angle-bracket depth negative and swallow the next real comma. No rule file touched.
